purpose: Trace the old Cagayan freshwater fish list toward its cited source and record later public research leads without treating a conference listing or regional production statistics as verified species occurrence data.

reviewedSources.finding: The official UP Visayas ICFAS 7 program guide lists Capt_Pos21, Provisional List of Freshwater Fish in Cagayan River, Cagayan Valley, Philippines, and names its authors. The PDF is the program guide, not the poster; no checklist, methods, dates, stations, vouchers, or coordinates could be examined.

NFRDI FiSearch says a paper titled Freshwater Fish Species in Cagayan River Basin, Philippines, by Melanie Villarao, Angel Encarnacion, Leon Antonio Jr., and Princess Jane Cansejo, was presented at the BFAR Region II CY 2024 Fisheries R&D Review. The notice has no underlying species data or sampling details.

The accessible BFAR Philippine Fisheries Profile 2006 is a national report, not demonstrated to be the BFAR Region II Profile 2006 cited by NEDA. It does not resolve the cited source or provide site-level fish observations.

The RDC Region II situationer provides historical production and aquaculture context, including broad inland-water and Magat Reservoir references. These are not standardized wild-fish sampling records, and no direct source chain to NEDA Table 9 was established.

sourceTrail.nedaTable9: NEDA's Cagayan Riverine Zone framework plan labels Table 9 an initial list of freshwater fish species along the Cagayan River as of 2006 and credits BFAR RO2 Profile 2006.
sourceTrail.jicaCrossCheck: The separately reviewed 2023 JICA report says its related Cagayan fish and shellfish list is based on a BFAR Region II 2006 survey. NEDA and JICA are repeated secondary renderings of the stated BFAR lineage, not independent surveys.
sourceTrail.unresolved: The underlying regional BFAR profile or survey was not retrieved. The national BFAR profile and RDC situationer do not substitute for that source.

interpretation: The 2023 poster listing and 2024 newsletter notice have different titles and author lists. Angel B. Encarnacion appears in both, but that overlap does not establish whether the projects are related or independent.
Neither conference notice is sufficient to add taxon-level occurrence, local distribution, abundance, or a species page to Bangwit.
Keep production, stocking, and aquaculture statistics distinct from observed natural occurrence.
limits: No full 2023 poster, 2024 conference paper or slides, underlying BFAR RO2 Profile 2006, voucher inventory, or site-by-taxon dataset was obtained.
No item-specific reuse terms were verified for the poster or presented study. Public access to a program guide or newsletter is not a reuse grant for study content.
No species or occurrence rows, coordinates, geometry, catch advice, regulation, safety claim, or public-app content was added; publication approval remains false.
next: Search public university and repository records for the full ICFAS poster and 2024 presentation, then compare any recovered methods and locality or voucher crosswalk against already-reviewed Cagayan-basin studies. Keep conference leads and production statistics separate from site-level occurrence evidence.
